bugs: Probe: a guest GET /api/webhook-events without an `Accept: application/json` header returns 500 with RouteNotFoundException 'Route [login] not defined'. Only the JSON path is tested.

routes/api.php:8 protects the admin API with the session-based `auth` (web guard) inside the stateless api group, and there is no Sanctum or token guard. In production an admin has no way to authenticate to the failed-events endpoint.

app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:64 uses firstOrFail for the order. A missing order is permanent, but its ModelNotFoundException is treated as transient. Probe: after the first run the event stays 'processing' with the job released, and it keeps retrying for about 40 minutes of backoff before it is marked failed.
app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:10: the receipt notification is not queued (it does not implement ShouldQueue), so mail is sent inline inside the job. A mail failure turns into a job retry.
The job has no DB transaction around the order update, refund creation and markAsProcessed, so a crash part-way leaves partially applied state. Retries are mostly idempotent, but it is not atomic.
The README says failed events can be replayed with `queue:retry`, but handle() returns early when the status is Failed, so a replay does nothing.
antipatterns: app/Notifications/PaymentReceipt.php:10 is a synchronous notification sent from a queued job, with no ShouldQueue or ShouldQueueAfterCommit
routes/api.php:8 uses the `auth` session guard on the stateless API, and `can:` is a string middleware rather than ->can()
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:64 uses firstOrFail for a permanent error instead of $this->fail()
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:74 writes the order's payment_details outside any transaction, and the related writes at lines 76-82 are not atomic
app/Http/Controllers/PaymentWebhookController.php:17 stores the whole validated() array as the payload, duplicating id and type
strengths: Cleanup uses MassPrunable with prunable() and a scheduled `model:prune` with onOneServer and withoutOverlapping, which is the idiomatic pruning setup
Unknown event types are still stored and accepted (200), then marked failed in the job, which matches 'store every event'

Order state transitions are guarded at the DB level (transitionFrom), so a late payment.succeeded or payment.failed cannot regress a refunded or paid order. receipt_sent_at guards against duplicate receipts.

Job attributes are used well: Backoff, MaxExceptions, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels and WithoutRelations, plus retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping per event, RateLimited, 429 Retry-After release and 4xx fail()

The tests are excellent. They run on a real database queue with `queue:work --once` and time travel, covering 5xx backoff, retry exhaustion leading to a failed event and failed_jobs, rate-limit release and overlap-lock release.
webhooks/* is added to shouldRenderJsonWhen, so validation errors return 422 JSON even without an Accept header
The signature check compares in constant time, normalises case and rejects an empty secret

bugs: Probe: a signed but invalid payload sent without an `Accept: application/json` header gets a 302 redirect instead of 422, because webhooks/* is not in shouldRenderJsonWhen (bootstrap/app.php:23). The tests always send an Accept header.

app/Http/Requests/StorePaymentWebhookRequest.php:16 uses Rule::enum on type, so unknown event types are rejected and never stored. That contradicts 'store every event exactly once', and the provider will keep retrying them.
app/Models/Order.php:42: markPaid only excludes Paid. Probe: a late payment.succeeded on a Refunded order flips it back to Paid and sends a receipt.

The redispatch command (every 10 minutes) re-queues any event still 'received' after 5 minutes. Under a rate-limited backlog this pushes duplicate jobs repeatedly. They are harmless thanks to the isFinished check and the lock, but they consume rate-limit slots.

app/Console/Commands/RedispatchReceivedWebhookEvents.php is extra machinery that the task does not require
tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:154 reconstructs the RateLimited middleware's internal md5 cache key
bootstrap/app.php:20: redirectGuestsTo with route('login') refers to a route that does not exist for non-API paths
strengths: Processing runs in DB::transaction with lockForUpdate on the order, and the receipt uses ShouldQueueAfterCommit, so the notification is queued and only sent after commit
The webhook dispatch uses ->afterCommit(), and createOrFirst on the unique event_id gives exactly-once storage
UnrecoverableWebhookException fails a missing order or a provider 4xx immediately via $this->fail(), while 5xx errors retry with Backoff, MaxExceptions and retryUntil
WithoutOverlapping per event and a shared RateLimited limiter, with the rate configurable through config
The admin API uses Sanctum, ->can() route authorization and a policy, so it is usable in production, and a guest without an Accept header gets 401
markPaid returns a bool so only the caller that made the transition sends the receipt, and a late payment.failed cannot downgrade a paid order
The README covers deployment thoroughly: shared cache, Supervisor, tries and timeout, retry_after, queue:restart and the scheduler
The tests are solid and Pest-idiomatic, using datasets and an end-to-end HTTP-to-processing test

v.rationale:
Both suites pass (impl-1: 38 tests, impl-2: 37). Each has sound core queue mechanics: createOrFirst on a unique event_id, WithoutOverlapping per event, a shared RateLimited limiter, Backoff and retryUntil, 4xx sent to fail(), a 429 Retry-After release, and failed() recording the error.

impl-2 ranks first, narrowly, because more of its parts work as they would in production:
- The order update, refund and event status change run in one transaction with a row lock.
- The receipt is queued and sent only after commit (ShouldQueueAfterCommit), and the webhook dispatch uses afterCommit.
- A missing order fails at once instead of retrying.
- The admin endpoint can actually be reached with a Sanctum token.

Its probed bugs:
- A 302 redirect instead of 422 for an invalid payload sent without an Accept header.
- Unknown event types are rejected and never stored.
- A refunded order can flip back to Paid when a late payment.succeeded arrives.
- It hand-rolls a prune command where MassPrunable would do, and adds an unrequested redispatch command.

impl-1 has the better pruning (MassPrunable with model:prune), stores unknown types, has safer order state transitions, and has outstanding real-queue tests. Its problems weigh more, though:
- The admin endpoint uses the session `auth` guard on the stateless API, so admins can't really authenticate. A guest request without an Accept header returns 500 ('Route [login] not defined').
- The receipt notification is synchronous.
- There is no transaction around the order, refund and event updates.
- A missing order is retried for about 40 minutes.
- The README says failed events can be replayed with queue:retry, but the job skips failed events, so the replay does nothing.
